publicFacts.fact: Capacity 200 MIGD by reverse osmosis; key facts give 909,201 m3/day (page text 909,200 m3/day). The live page returned 404 on 2026-10-24, so it was read from the Internet Archive snapshot of 2026-10-17
Offtaker EWEC under a 30-year water purchase agreement; project cost US$907 million; commercial operations date Q1 2024
ACWA Power share 40%; other investors Mubadala and TAQA; project company Taweelah RO Desalination Company; EPC SEPCOIII and Abengoa Agua
Phase 1 began operating in June 2022 at 454.6 thousand m3/day (100 MIGD); connected to the grid in December 2021
Phase 2 declared in commercial operation in April 2023; total 909,218 m3/day; photovoltaic field of more than 70 MWp; plant sits in the Taweelah power and water complex, 45 km from Abu Dhabi
Passed 30 consecutive days of final tests and produced 204 MIGD in one day (2% above plan); named Desalination Plant of the Year 2023 at the Global Water Awards
IDOM carried out basic and detailed engineering for SEPCOIII; associated PV plant of 70 MWp

Footprint about 379,000 m2 in the southern portion of the Taweelah Power & Water Complex. Components: open-channel seawater intake with breakwaters, 3 km piped outfall, RO plant, potable-water storage tanks, solar PV (ground- and roof-mounted)
9 potable-water storage tanks east of the site (to be operated by EWEC): 6 x 105 m diameter x 17.8 m high and 3 x 77 m diameter x 17.5 m high
PV was to be placed on the tank roofs and the former laydown area as well as around the RO plant; the plant buildings run diagonally across the site, surrounded by PV
Site bordered to the S and W by the Taweelah Complex outfall channel; Khalifa Port ~2 km N; EGA alumina refinery ~4 km NE; KIZAD Area A ~2.5 km NE; new structures described as low-rise
Conflicting published figures: capacity 909,200 / 909,201 / 909,216 / 909,218 m3/day; cost US$907 m vs US$874 m; PV 40 MW / ~50 MW / ~69 MW / >70 MWp. None is exact; treat as a range

exteriorFeatures: Kite/diamond plot of ~0.35-0.38 km2 rotated ~45 deg: NW edge on the beach (~710 m), NE edge on the complex road (~640 m), SE edge on a channel (~470 m), SW edge on the outfall channel (~590 m)

Buildings on a true-north grid, set diagonally inside the plot: 2 north halls, a row of 4 halls, a long central hall, 2 grey-roofed service buildings, a long south hall. 8 large flat halls in total, all with PV-covered roofs (grid of panel blocks, white walkways, white roof edges)
Each hall in the row of 4 has a white-roofed annex (~23 m deep) on its south side; 2 small white-roofed ancillary blocks east of the central hall

Ground-mounted PV over most remaining land: long N-S strips ~18-20 m wide with ~1 m gaps and sawtooth ends along the plot edges. Gable-shaped row ends suggest east-west dual-tilt racking (inferred, unconfirmed)

Seawater intake at the N tip: hooked west rubble breakwater (~320 m) and straight east arm (~200 m) enclosing a calm basin (~120 x 150 m) with a floating boom; beige concrete intake structures on the shore
Small colour accents: 2 red-orange round tanks (~8-9 m dia) near the intake; white dome-roofed round tanks (~16-18 m dia) beside the central and south halls; small silver silos
Open rectangular basins with visible greenish water just west of the north-west hall
Teal cooling-water outfall channels (~60 m wide, sandy levees) wrap the SW and SE edges; Arabian Gulf to the NW with a sandy beach
Neighbours: old Taweelah A1/A2/B gas power and MSF desalination plants immediately NE (long evaporator rows, stacks, white tanks); Khalifa Port ~2 km N; EGA aluminium complex ~4 km NE

Off-site, ~1.1 km ESE: 9 giant flat-roofed potable-water tanks (6 x 105 m, 3 x 77 m, 17.5-17.8 m high) with PV-covered roofs in a rounded dark-paved enclosure (~390 x 300 m); a kite-shaped PV block (~490 x 630 m) just south of it (inferred former laydown area)

modelingBrief.massing: Flat diamond plot carpeted with dark PV rows, holding an orthogonal north-aligned column of similar-height flat-roofed halls (2 + 4 + 1 + 1, plus 2 lower service blocks). Hooked rubble breakwater and basin at the north tip; teal channels on the SW and SE; open Gulf to the NW; a cluster of 9 giant round tanks ~1.1 km ESE. Local frame: metres East/North of 24.7585, 54.6748.
modelingBrief.estimatedDimensions: All estimates, +/-10-15 m. Halls are axis-aligned to true north. North halls N1/N2: centres (-81,+218), (+11,+218); ~67 x 110 m; ~18-25 m high (uncertain). Halls A-D: centres (-162/-75/+11/+97, +71); ~73 x 102 m each, including a ~23 m white south annex; ~18-19 m high. Central long hall: (+46,-58); ~173 x 69 m; ~15-20 m. Service buildings: (+5,-120) ~107 x 40 m and (+133,-120) ~108 x 45 m; ~10-14 m. South long hall: (+54,-184); ~172 x 68 m; ~15-20 m. White ancillary blocks: (+177,-44), (+177,-74); ~67 x 24 m; ~6-10 m. Intake structures: (-99,+359); ~110 x 70 m. West breakwater: root (-162,+328) to head (-315,+598). East breakwater: root (-47,+424) to head (-222,+516). Plot corners: N (-83,+453), E (+389,+16), S (+101,-354), W (-472,-155). Ground PV ~1-2.5 m high. Tank farm centre (+1118,-632): 6 x 105 m dia x 17.8 m and 3 x 77 m dia x 17.5 m (tank sizes sourced from the ESIA). Kite PV block centre (+1124,-1199), ~490 x 630 m. Hall heights come from shadows calibrated against the 17.8 m tanks.
palette: #1F7F78 outfall channel water, render value (sampled darker ~#145A4E)
#8A8C78 hall cladding as drawn in the 2020 IDOM render (as-built unverified)
modelingBrief.materials: Flat roofs with PV module texture and walkway lines; metal-clad hall walls (colour unverified); steel tanks with white rims and PV roofs; rough grey rubble breakwaters; asphalt roads; sand ground; water with gentle normal maps.
modelingBrief.surroundings: NW: open Arabian Gulf and a sandy beach. NE: dense old Taweelah power/MSF desalination complex. ~2 km N: Khalifa Port. ~4 km NE: EGA aluminium complex. S/SE: channels, sandy plots and tree plantations. ESE: 9-tank farm and kite PV block. Inland: desert and KIZAD industrial plots.
modelingBrief.unknowns: Unknown or illustrative: exact hall heights, rooflines and parapets; facade colours/materials of the as-built halls; which building houses which process (not public, so use neutral labels such as 'Process hall A' and keep any process labels fictional); PV racking type; whether the kite PV block belongs to the project; intake structure form; tank-farm enclosure details; night lighting. Do not model gates, fences, security posts, cable/pipeline routes or interiors.

publicFacts.fact: Joint venture of Mubadala and Cleveland Clinic (2006 agreement); opened 2015, officially inaugurated 3 Dec 2015; part of the M42 network since 2023
411 beds (321 acute, 90 critical care), expandable to 490; five clinical floors, three diagnostic and treatment levels and 13 inpatient floors; 23-acre facility
Height 99.6 m (327 ft); 24 floors above ground; completed 2015 (construction started 2009); composite structure

Design architect HDR (selected through an international design competition); architect of record Aedas; structural/MEP AECOM; main contractor Samsung C&T (CTBUH also lists Six Construct); developer Aldar Properties

2,300,000 sf (213,676 m2), LEED Gold. Each healthcare component has its own stacked architectural form; diamond-patterned glazing references Islamic geometry; glass echoes the sea; onyx-toned elements reference the desert
A double-skinned curtain wall wraps the patient tower, with a nearly 5 ft (~1.5 m) air gap between the outer and inner skins
Described as the largest structural-steel building in the UAE (>30,000 t). Wikipedia gives 422,681 m2 of floor space, which conflicts with HDR/CTBUH's 213,676 m2
Fatima bint Mubarak Center (cancer care) opened March 2023, 205,000 sq ft; the 2022 topping-off release gives 19,000 m2 and mentions the final glass panel on the tenth floor
The Aedas landscape page given in the brief returned 404 on 2026-10-24 and has no Wayback copy; its content could not be verified

exteriorFeatures: Stacked-box composition: separate rectangular volumes, each with its own cladding (HDR: 'each healthcare component occupies its own architectural form')

Top: a long N-S inpatient glass slab (~128 x 41 m in plan, ~13 storeys) with its long face west towards the water, wrapped in a double-skin diamond-lattice curtain wall of teal-green glass; narrow darker vertical slot near one end
Dark recessed transfer band beneath the slab, so the slab appears to float

Two mid-level E-W diamond-glazed bars (~4 storeys): the north bar (~142 x 35 m) extends west and cantilevers towards the waterfront, with a rooftop helipad (green pad, white H); the south bar (~119 x 40 m) extends east. The slab rests across both in a pinwheel/Z plan
Gold / 'onyx'-toned patterned block (~125 x 50 m) under the north bar, with punched windows and a green roof garden on its exposed south part; reads gold by day, copper-brown at dusk
Long low fully glazed waterfront podium (~264 x 25 m, 4-5 storeys) along a curved promenade with palms; a lower 2-storey glass pavilion with a grass roof to its NW
Grey metal-clad central base (~117 x 114 m) with a landscaped courtyard
North entrance: glass cube, curving drop-off and tree-lined plazas; a broad lawn terrace slopes to the promenade; tree-lined park on the east side
Fatima bint Mubarak Center (cancer centre, 2023) at the south end, ~78 x 77 m in plan, height unconfirmed
Campus grid rotated ~7 deg clockwise from north; at night the diamond pattern is lit violet-blue in HDR's photos

modelingBrief.massing: Extruded boxes, rotated ~7 deg clockwise, local frame in metres East/North of 24.4971, 54.3879. Waterfront podium (-95,+28) 264 x 25 m; pavilion (-110,+103) 166 x 41 m; gold block (-56,+74) 125 x 50 m; grey base (+25,+51) 117 x 114 m; north bar (-31,+100) 142 x 35 m, E-W; south bar (+49,+19) 119 x 40 m, E-W; inpatient slab (+14,+59) 128 x 41 m, N-S; cancer centre (+10,-81) 78 x 77 m. Footprints from OSM (ODbL).
modelingBrief.estimatedDimensions: Total height 99.6 m (CTBUH, sourced). Recommended split (estimates reconciled with photos): podium 0-20 m; pavilion 0-10 m; gold block 0-32 m; grey base 0-25 m; north and south bars ~32-50 m; recessed transfer band ~50-54 m (inset 3-5 m); slab ~54-99.6 m (~13 storeys; outer diamond skin ~1.5 m off the inner wall); cancer centre ~40-45 m (unconfirmed). The OSM community heights differ (bars 25-60 m, slab 60-110 m) and overshoot CTBUH.
palette: #E2C592 gold/onyx block panels by day (sampled; mid #8A7756, window voids #303D3A)
modelingBrief.materials: Two-layer glass on the slab (outer diamond mullion lattice over a reflective inner curtain wall); same diamond glazing on the bars, slightly greener; matte patterned panels with punched windows on the gold block; teal curtain wall with horizontal mullions on the podium; grey metal panels on the base; green roof gardens; generic helipad decal; no logos.
modelingBrief.surroundings: W: curved waterfront promenade with palms, then a turquoise channel (~150 m wide) and Abu Dhabi island (Al Zahiyah/Tourist Club area) with a beach and hotels. N: Sowwah Square / ADGM dark-glass towers and The Galleria (general geography). Road bridges cross the channel just N and S of the campus. E: tree-lined park, arterial road and the Al Maryah business district. NE: Al Reem Island across a second channel.
modelingBrief.unknowns: Unknown or illustrative: exact storey heights per volume (both splits are estimates); transfer-band inset and cantilever lengths; diamond-lattice module size; gold-block pattern; cancer-centre height and facade; rooftop equipment; night-lighting colours (vary by event). Do not model interiors, detailed entrances, security/emergency access or logos.

publicFacts.fact: State-of-the-art 132/11 kV digital substation (Nad Hessa), inspected by DEWA's MD & CEO; news dated 12 May 2025
Total capacity 150 MVA
Cost over AED 93.322 million; 649,064 safe man-hours with zero injuries; completed five months ahead of schedule
Facilities integrated into a single building to minimise the built-up area
57% CO2 reduction (54.24 t/yr); Green Apple Environment Award 2023, Green World Award 2023, Emirates Innovates Award for digital substation design
DEWA commissioned 8 new 132 kV substations in H1 2024 at locations including 'Nadd Hessa'. Likely the same substation, but not explicitly stated
DEWA's standardised digital 132 kV design (generic, not Nad Hessa-specific) saves ~220 m2 of construction area per substation
Nadd Hessa community: 9.8 km2, population 40,819 (2022)
